data.analysis: Keep N=2 and both role identities. The approaches are meaningfully distinct: CTA-level shared-memory reordering versus warp-local register/shuffle exchange. One shared, unverified hypothesis is that the baseline’s lane-strided stores dominate the n=1024 timing; its correct three-sample mean is 16.919 µs, but there are no candidate measurements or hardware-counter evidence. Refine T1 to contrast layouts rather than presuming the padded scalar tile is best, and refine T2 to make warp-local ownership explicit rather than assuming shuffles cross warps.

revisions.objective: Own only src/candidate.cu. Replace the baseline's strided global stores with a single-pass shared-memory tiled transpose: load input rows coalesced, exchange tile orientation in shared memory, then store output rows coalesced. Compare the padded 32x33 scalar tile with at least one meaningfully different shared-memory layout or multi-element/vectorized thread-ownership variant; do not presume the padded scalar layout is fastest on this target. Measure the complete run at n=1024. Preserve the run entry point and exact bit patterns; produce every C element for every positive n multiple of 32, pass correctness at n=32, 64, 256, and 1024, use no new allocation or other file edits, and report build, correctness, and repeated timing evidence.
revisions.subject: Shared-memory transpose layouts and ownership

revisions.objective: Own only src/candidate.cu. Independently explore a warp-register transpose using warp lane permutations/shuffles to turn coalesced input loads into coalesced output stores, aiming to avoid CTA shared-memory staging and its block-wide synchronization. Design and describe element ownership so each shuffle exchange uses data held by participating lanes in the same warp; do not assume a warp shuffle exchanges data across warps. Tune the warp's element ownership and tile mapping, and report register/spill evidence if present in the ordinary build output. Preserve exact bitwise copies and the run entry point, produce all output for every positive n multiple of 32, pass the required correctness sizes, allocate no new storage, and report repeated full-run n=1024 timing evidence.
revisions.subject: Warp-local register/shuffle transpose

data.shared_assumptions: Both missions hypothesize that improving the baseline’s strided C stores will help at n=1024; validate this with repeated timings under the unchanged protocol rather than treating it as proven. Keep all dimensions that are positive multiples of 32 correct, preserve bit patterns, and compare only correctly validated programs. The supplied target is GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3; no additional architecture capability is assumed.
